question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with initial velocity (u). After time (t), its velocity (v) becomes __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is v = u − gt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a ball thrown vertically upward, gravity acts downward, opposing the motion, so it is taken as a retarding (negative) acceleration. Using the first equation of motion v = u + at with a = −g, we get v = u − gt. (ऊपर फेंकी गई गेंद — गुरुत्व त्वरण ऋणात्मक)

 

• As the ball rises, its speed keeps decreasing until it becomes zero at the highest point, after which it falls back with increasing speed.

 

• Time to reach maximum height: t = u/g. Maximum height reached: h = u²/2g.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three equations of motion for uniform acceleration: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as.

 

• For a freely falling body (dropped from rest), u = 0, and acceleration is +g (downward), so v = gt.

 

• The value of g on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s².

 

NOTE

 

• v = gt − uv (Option B) and v = u·gtv (Option C) are not dimensionally or physically valid equations of motion.

 

• v = u + gt (Option D) would be correct only if the ball were falling downward with gravity aiding the motion, not for upward motion.

question: In animals, sensitivity or responsiveness is mainly controlled by the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is nervous system.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The nervous system is responsible for sensitivity and responsiveness in animals — it detects stimuli through receptors and coordinates a rapid response. (तंत्रिका तंत्र — संवेदनशीलता एवं अनुक्रिया)

 

• It is made up of the brain, spinal cord and nerves, and its basic functional unit is the neuron, which carries electrical impulses.

 

• The nervous system works alongside the endocrine system (hormones) to control and coordinate body activities, but the nervous system's response is much faster because it uses electrical signals rather than chemical messengers travelling through blood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The human nervous system is divided into the Central Nervous System (CNS) — brain and spinal cord — and the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS) — all the nerves branching out from the CNS.

 

• The pathway of a quick involuntary response is called a reflex arc, e.g., withdrawing a hand from a hot object.

 

• Plants, which lack a nervous system, show responsiveness through tropisms (like phototropism, geotropism) controlled by hormones such as auxin.

 

NOTE

 

• Respiratory system (Option A): Involved in the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide, not in sensing stimuli.

 

• Digestive system (Option B): Breaks down food into absorbable nutrients.

 

• Circulatory system (Option C): Transports blood, nutrients, gases and hormones throughout the body.

question: Which of the following is a component of phloem tissue?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sieve tubes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Phloem is a complex, living conducting tissue in plants that transports prepared food (mainly sucrose) from the leaves to other parts of the plant, a process called translocation. (फ्लोएम — भोजन का संवहन)

 

• Phloem is made up of four components: sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres. Sieve tubes are the main conducting elements, made of living cells joined end to end with perforated sieve plates.

 

• Companion cells lie alongside sieve tubes and help regulate their activity, since mature sieve tube cells lose their nucleus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Xylem, by contrast, is a dead conducting tissue that transports water and minerals upward from roots to leaves, a unidirectional flow.

 

• Xylem is composed of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres; of these, only xylem parenchyma is living.

 

• Together, xylem and phloem form the vascular bundles of a plant, and the tissue responsible for their formation is the vascular cambium.

 

NOTE

 

• Tracheids (Option B): Dead, elongated cells with tapering ends, part of the xylem, used for water conduction.

 

• Xylem fibres (Option C): Provide mechanical support in the xylem tissue.

 

• Vessels (Option D): Tube-like dead xylem cells that conduct water efficiently.

question: Where does fertilisation usually occur in the female reproductive system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oviduct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fertilisation — the fusion of a sperm and an egg (ovum) — usually occurs in the oviduct (Fallopian tube), specifically in its wider outer part called the ampulla. (डिंबवाहिनी नली — निषेचन का स्थान)

 

• The oviduct connects the ovary to the uterus. After fertilisation, the resulting zygote divides repeatedly as it travels down the oviduct and implants itself in the uterus for further development.

 

• Each month, one ovary releases a mature egg during ovulation; the egg is swept into the oviduct by finger-like projections called fimbriae.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The uterus (womb) is the pear-shaped organ where the fertilised egg implants and the foetus develops until birth.

 

• The cervix is the narrow lower end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

 

• The vagina is the muscular canal that forms the birth canal and receives sperm during copulation.

 

NOTE

 

• Uterus (Option A): The site of implantation and foetal development, not fertilisation.

 

• Cervix (Option C): The passage connecting the uterus and vagina.

 

• Vagina (Option D): The external opening of the female reproductive tract.

question: Which of the following experimental observations provides the strongest evidence for the existence of particles in matter?
option_2: Salt dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water
option_3: Ice melts into water when heated
option_4: A drop of ink spreads evenly in water without stirring
solution_text:
The correct answer is A drop of ink spreads evenly in water without stirring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The spontaneous, uniform spreading of ink in still water is a classic demonstration of diffusion, which occurs because matter is made of tiny, discrete, constantly-moving particles with empty spaces between them. (विसरण — कणों के अस्तित्व का प्रमाण)

 

• Since the ink particles move on their own (without stirring) and mix completely with water particles, this is the strongest direct evidence that matter is particulate in nature — solid continuous matter could not do this.

 

• Diffusion is faster in gases, slower in liquids, and slowest in solids, because particle spacing and speed of movement decrease from gases to solids.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Boiling and melting show a change of state due to particles gaining energy and overcoming intermolecular forces, but these processes alone don't demonstrate the particulate, moving nature of matter as vividly as diffusion does.

 

• Brownian motion — the random zig-zag movement of pollen grains or smoke particles suspended in a fluid — is another key evidence for the kinetic (particle) theory of matter.

 

• The kinetic theory of matter states that all matter is composed of particles that are in continuous, random motion and possess kinetic energy that increases with temperature.

 

NOTE

 

• Water boils and produces steam (Option A): Shows a change of state (liquid to gas) due to heating, not direct evidence of particle spacing/motion.

 

• Salt dissolves faster in warm water (Option B): Shows that higher temperature increases particle kinetic energy and speeds up dissolution, but is a secondary rather than the most direct evidence.

 

• Ice melts into water when heated (Option C): Shows a change of state (solid to liquid), again a consequence rather than direct proof of particle existence.

question: Which of the following industries uses sodium hydroxide for processing wood pulp?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paper Industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), also called caustic soda, is used in the paper industry to process wood pulp — it dissolves lignin (the substance that binds wood fibres together) so that the cellulose fibres can be separated and used to make paper. (सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड — कागज उद्योग में लुगदी प्रसंस्करण)

 

• This chemical process, called the kraft (sulphate) process or soda process, helps produce strong, pure cellulose fibre pulp used for paper manufacturing.

 

• NaOH is a strong alkali (base) manufactured mainly by the chlor-alkali process through electrolysis of brine (saturated sodium chloride solution).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major uses of sodium hydroxide: making soap and detergents, artificial silk (rayon), degreasing metals, and as a laboratory reagent.

 

• The chlor-alkali process electrolyses brine to give three useful products: chlorine gas (Cl₂) at the anode, hydrogen gas (H₂) at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution.

 

• Chlorine from this process is used to make bleaching powder and PVC; hydrogen is used in the manufacture of ammonia and as a fuel.

 

NOTE

 

• Food Industry (Option A): Uses NaOH in small controlled amounts (e.g., for pretzel/olive processing) but this is not its defining industrial application.

 

• Soap Industry (Option C): Also uses NaOH (in saponification of fats/oils to make hard soap), but the specific use for wood pulp processing belongs to the paper industry.

 

• Textile Industry (Option D): Uses NaOH for mercerisation of cotton fabric to improve strength and lustre, not for wood pulp.

question: The angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray of a prism is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Angle of deviation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The angle of deviation (δ) is the angle between the original direction of the incident ray and the direction of the emergent ray after it passes through a prism — it measures how much the prism has bent the light overall. (विचलन कोण — आपतित एवं निर्गत किरण के मध्य कोण)

 

• Light bends twice while passing through a prism: once while entering (refraction at the first surface) and once while leaving (refraction at the second surface); the angle of deviation is the net/cumulative effect of both bendings.

 

• The angle of deviation depends on the angle of incidence, the refracting angle of the prism, and the refractive index of the prism material; it is minimum for a specific angle of incidence, called the angle of minimum deviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Angle of refraction is the angle the refracted ray makes with the normal inside the prism at the point of entry.

 

• Angle of emergence is the angle the emergent ray makes with the normal at the point where light exits the prism.

 

• A prism splits white light into its seven constituent colours (VIBGYOR) through dispersion, because each colour has a slightly different refractive index and hence a different angle of deviation.

 

NOTE

 

• Angle of refraction (Option B): Concerns bending at a single surface, measured from the normal, not the overall path change.

 

• Angle of emergence (Option C): The angle at which light leaves the second surface, again measured from the normal at that surface.

 

• Angle of incidence (Option D): The angle at which the original ray strikes the first surface of the prism.

question: According to Thomson's model of an atom, which of the following statements best describes the structure of the atom?
option_1: Electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere.
option_2: The atom contains only neutrons and electrons.
option_3: Electrons revolve around a central nucleus in fixed orbits.
option_4: The atom consists of a dense nucleus surrounded by electrons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electrons are embedded in a positively charged sphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• J.J. Thomson's atomic model (1904), often called the "plum pudding model", proposed that an atom is a sphere of uniform positive charge with negatively charged electrons embedded in it, like seeds in a watermelon or plums in a pudding. (थॉमसन का परमाणु मॉडल — प्लम पुडिंग मॉडल)

 

• In this model, the positive and negative charges are equal in magnitude, making the atom electrically neutral overall, and the mass is assumed to be uniformly distributed throughout the sphere.

 

• Thomson had earlier discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode ray experiments, which led him to propose this model to explain how a negatively charged particle could exist within a neutral atom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Thomson's model was disproved by Ernest Rutherford's gold foil (alpha-scattering) experiment (1911), which showed that most of an atom's mass and positive charge is concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

 

• Rutherford's model described electrons revolving around the nucleus in space, like planets around the sun, but could not explain why electrons don't spiral into the nucleus.

 

• Niels Bohr (1913) improved on this by proposing that electrons revolve in fixed, defined orbits (energy levels) without radiating energy.

 

NOTE

 

• The atom contains only neutrons and electrons (Option B): Incorrect — atoms also contain positively charged protons; in fact, neutrons weren't even discovered until 1932 (by Chadwick), long after Thomson's model.

 

• Electrons revolve around a central nucleus in fixed orbits (Option C): This describes Bohr's model, not Thomson's.

 

• The atom consists of a dense nucleus surrounded by electrons (Option D): This describes Rutherford's model, not Thomson's.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of action and reaction forces?
option_1: Foot pushes the ground backward and ground pushes the foot forward
option_2: A rocket moving upward due to gases expelled downward
option_3: When the bus stops suddenly, people fall forward
option_4: The swimmer pushes the water backward with her hands
solution_text:
The correct answer is When the bus stops suddenly, people fall forward.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's Third Law of Motion states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction, and these two forces act on two different bodies simultaneously. (न्यूटन का तीसरा नियम — क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया)

 

• A person falling forward when a bus stops suddenly is explained by Newton's First Law (the law of inertia), not the third law — the person's body tends to continue moving forward at the bus's original speed even though the bus (and their feet) have stopped, because a body in motion resists a change in its state of motion. (जड़त्व का नियम)

 

• This is a case of a single force imbalance causing a change of motion, not a mutual action-reaction pair between two bodies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's Laws of Motion: First Law (inertia) — a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force; Second Law — F = ma; Third Law — action and reaction are equal, opposite, and act on different bodies.

 

• Everyday examples of action-reaction pairs: walking (foot pushes ground back, ground pushes foot forward), swimming, rowing a boat, a gun recoiling when fired, and rockets/jet engines expelling gas.

 

• A common trick to identify Newton's third law: check if the two forces act on two different objects — if yes, it's action-reaction; if the same object experiences unbalanced forces causing it to speed up, slow down or change direction, it is usually the first or second law at play.

 

NOTE

 

• Foot pushes ground / ground pushes foot (Option A): A textbook action-reaction pair enabling walking.

 

• Rocket propulsion (Option B): Gases are pushed downward and backward (action); the rocket is pushed upward/forward (reaction) — a genuine action-reaction pair.

 

• Swimmer pushing water (Option D): The swimmer pushes water backward (action); water pushes the swimmer forward (reaction) — also a genuine action-reaction pair.

question: What is the purpose of cross-breeding exotic and local cattle breeds?
option_1: To make animals smaller in size
option_2: To make the animals more aggressive
option_3: To combine long lactation with disease resistance
solution_text:
The correct answer is To combine long lactation with disease resistance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cross-breeding of exotic (foreign) and indigenous (local) cattle breeds aims to combine the desirable traits of both: the long lactation period and high milk yield of exotic breeds (like Jersey and Holstein-Friesian) with the disease resistance and heat tolerance of local Indian breeds (like Sahiwal and Red Sindhi). (संकरण — विदेशी एवं देशी नस्लों के गुणों का संयोजन)

 

• Exotic breeds generally give more milk but are less resistant to Indian climatic conditions and local diseases, while indigenous breeds are hardier but produce less milk — cross-breeding balances these two aspects to raise overall productivity.

 

• This falls under Animal Husbandry, the branch of agriculture dealing with the care, breeding and management of livestock to improve their quality and productivity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Animal breeding methods: Inbreeding (mating within the same breed to improve desirable traits and increase homozygosity) and out-breeding (mating unrelated animals — including cross-breeding and inter-species hybridisation, such as a mule from a horse and donkey).

 

• India's National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) has promoted cross-breeding programmes to improve milk yield, most famously through Operation Flood, which made India the world's largest milk producer.

 

• Well-known Indian (Zebu) cattle breeds: Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Gir, Tharparkar; well-known exotic breeds: Jersey, Holstein-Friesian, Brown Swiss.

 

NOTE

 

• To make animals smaller in size (Option A): Not a goal of cross-breeding; productivity, not size reduction, is the aim.

 

• To make the animals more aggressive (Option B): Irrelevant and undesirable for dairy/farm animals.

 

• To reduce food requirements (Option D): Cross-bred animals are managed for better feed-conversion efficiency, but reducing food intake is not the primary purpose.

question: The pH of four different solutions are given in the options. Which of them will turn red litmus blue?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A solution with pH greater than 7 is basic (alkaline) in nature, and a basic solution turns red litmus paper blue. Among the given values, only pH 11 is greater than 7. (क्षारीय विलयन — लाल लिटमस को नीला करता है)

 

• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14: pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, and pH > 7 is basic. It was devised by the Danish chemist S.P.L. Sørensen.

 

• Litmus is a natural dye (extracted from lichens) commonly used as an acid-base indicator: acids turn blue litmus red, while bases turn red litmus blue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• pH 4 and pH 2 (Options A and D) are acidic (less than 7) and would turn blue litmus red, not affect red litmus.

 

• pH 6 (Option C) is also acidic (slightly below neutral 7), so it too would not turn red litmus blue.

 

• Common pH values: lemon juice ≈ 2, pure water = 7 (neutral), soap solution ≈ 9-10, milk of magnesia ≈ 10, human blood ≈ 7.4.

 

NOTE

 

• pH 4 (Option A): Acidic; would turn blue litmus red.

 

• pH 6 (Option C): Weakly acidic (close to neutral); would not turn red litmus blue.

 

• pH 2 (Option D): Strongly acidic; would turn blue litmus red.

question: Which of the following statements best describes allotropes of carbon?
option_1: They are different isotopes of carbon with varying numbers of neutrons.
option_2: They are isomers of carbon, having the same molecular formula but different structures.
option_3: They are compounds formed by carbon with different elements.
option_4: They are different structural forms of carbon with different physical properties but similar chemical properties.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are different structural forms of carbon with different physical properties but similar chemical properties.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Allotropes are different structural (physical) forms of the same element, arising because the atoms are arranged differently. They show different physical properties (like hardness, appearance, conductivity) but essentially similar chemical properties, since they are made of the same atoms. (अपररूप — कार्बन के विभिन्न रूप)

 

• The major crystalline allotropes of carbon are diamond, graphite and fullerene (buckminsterfullerene, C₆₀); amorphous forms include coal, coke, charcoal and soot.

 

• In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms in a rigid three-dimensional tetrahedral structure, making it the hardest known natural substance. In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three others in flat hexagonal layers, which can slide over each other, making graphite soft and a good lubricant/conductor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diamond does not conduct electricity (no free electrons), while graphite conducts electricity because each carbon atom leaves one free (delocalised) electron.

 

• Fullerenes are cage-like, hollow molecules of carbon (like C₆₀, shaped like a football/football-soccer ball), discovered in 1985, for which Kroto, Curl and Smalley won the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

 

• Other classic allotrope examples: oxygen (O₂) and ozone (O₃); red, white and black phosphorus; rhombic and monoclinic sulphur.

 

NOTE

 

• Isotopes (Option A): Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons (e.g., Carbon-12 and Carbon-14) — a nuclear, not structural, distinction.

 

• Isomers (Option B): Different compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement — a concept in organic chemistry, not applicable to a single element's allotropes.

 

• Compounds with different elements (Option C): This describes chemical compounds of carbon (like CO₂ or CaCO₃), not allotropes, which involve carbon alone.

question: A force (F) of 10 N is applied on a body, causing it to move 5 m in the direction of the force. The work done (W) is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done is defined as the product of force applied and the displacement of the body in the direction of the force: W = F × d. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन)

 

• Here, F = 10 N and d = 5 m, and since the body moves in the same direction as the force, the angle between them is 0°, so W = F × d = 10 × 5 = 50 J.

 

• The SI unit of work is the joule (J), where 1 joule = 1 newton × 1 metre. Work is a scalar quantity (it has magnitude only, no direction).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general formula for work when force and displacement are at an angle θ is W = F·d·cos θ. Work is zero when θ = 90° (force perpendicular to displacement), and negative when θ > 90° (force opposes displacement).

 

• Power is the rate of doing work: P = W/t, measured in watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second.

 

• Energy is the capacity to do work and is also measured in joules; the work-energy theorem states that the work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to just add or subtract F and d (giving 15 J or 5 J) instead of multiplying them — always remember W = F × d, not F + d.

 

• 2 J (Option A) and 15 J (Option C) do not correspond to any valid formula involving the given values.

question: Which of the following is a safe sex method to help prevent the transmission of HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Using condoms during sexual intercourse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) spreads mainly through unprotected sexual contact, transfusion of infected blood, sharing of infected needles/syringes, and from an infected mother to her child. Using a condom during sexual intercourse acts as a physical barrier that prevents the exchange of body fluids (semen, vaginal fluid, blood) and is one of the most effective ways to reduce the risk of transmission. (कंडोम — एचआईवी संचरण रोकथाम)

 

• HIV attacks the body's immune system, specifically destroying CD4+ T-helper lymphocytes, and its advanced stage is called AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome).

 

• HIV does NOT spread by casual contact such as shaking hands, hugging, sharing food, or mosquito bites — this is a commonly tested misconception.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other preventive measures against HIV: using sterile, disposable needles/syringes, screening blood before transfusion, and avoiding sharing of razors or other objects that may carry blood.

 

• World AIDS Day is observed on 1 December every year to raise awareness.

 

• HIV is diagnosed through the ELISA test and Western blot test; antiretroviral therapy (ART) can control the virus but there is currently no permanent cure.

 

NOTE

 

• Taking multivitamins regularly (Option A): Supports general health but has no role in preventing HIV transmission.

 

• Sharing needles carefully (Option B): Sharing needles under any circumstances carries a high risk of HIV transmission; needles should never be shared, not just used "carefully".

 

• Taking antibiotics after sex (Option D): Antibiotics act against bacteria, not viruses like HIV, so they offer no protection.

question: Seed dispersal is important for plants because it:
solution_text:
The correct answer is prevents overcrowding and competition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Seed dispersal is the process by which seeds are scattered away from the parent plant, and it is important mainly because it prevents overcrowding of seedlings around the parent plant and reduces competition among them for sunlight, water, and nutrients. (बीज प्रकीर्णन — भीड़ एवं प्रतिस्पर्धा से बचाव)

 

• Dispersal also allows plants to colonise new areas, reduces the chance that seeds/seedlings will be eaten by the same predators or affected by the same diseases concentrated near the parent plant, and helps a species spread over a wider geographical range.

 

• Seeds are dispersed by different agents: wind (light, winged, or hairy seeds like those of maple and dandelion), water (buoyant seeds like coconut), animals (via fur, fruit consumption, or spines, like burrs and mango seeds), and explosive mechanisms (self-dispersal, like in pea pods and castor).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fertilisation occurs when a male gamete (from pollen) fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote, which develops into an embryo inside the seed — the seed is very much alive, not dead, after fertilisation.

 

• Pollination (transfer of pollen from anther to stigma) happens before fertilisation and seed formation, and is a separate, essential process — seed dispersal does not prevent it.

 

• After dispersal and under favourable conditions (adequate water, oxygen and suitable temperature), a seed undergoes germination to develop into a new plant.

 

NOTE

 

• Ensures seed death after fertilisation (Option B): Factually incorrect — fertilisation leads to seed and embryo formation, not death.

 

• Prevents pollination (Option C): Seed dispersal occurs after pollination and fertilisation are already complete; it has no role in preventing pollination.

 

• Increases the size of seeds (Option D): Seed size is determined by genetic and developmental factors, not by the dispersal process.

question: Which statement DOES NOT relate to the versatile nature of carbon?.
option_1: It can have single, double, and triple bonds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It can bond ionically.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbon's "versatile nature" refers to its unique ability to form a huge number of compounds, arising from properties like tetravalency, catenation, and the ability to form single, double and triple bonds. Carbon does NOT typically bond ionically — this is the property that does not relate to its versatility. (कार्बन की चतुःसंयोजकता — सहसंयोजक आबंधन)

 

• Carbon has 4 valence electrons, and because it needs to share (not completely gain or lose) 4 electrons to complete its octet, it almost always forms strong covalent bonds rather than ionic bonds — losing or gaining 4 electrons to form ions (C⁴⁺ or C⁴⁻) would require far too much energy and is not energetically favourable.

 

• Because carbon shares electrons covalently, it forms compounds with a huge variety of elements as well as with itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Catenation is the unique ability of carbon atoms to form long chains, branched chains, and rings by bonding with other carbon atoms, which (along with tetravalency) explains the existence of millions of organic compounds.

 

• Carbon can form single (C-C), double (C=C) and triple (C≡C) covalent bonds, giving rise to saturated (alkanes) and unsaturated (alkenes, alkynes) hydrocarbons.

 

• Covalent bonds are generally strong and stable, which is one reason carbon compounds (from methane to DNA) are so structurally robust and abundant in living systems.

 

NOTE

 

• Single, double and triple bonds (Option A): A genuine feature of carbon's versatility, seen in alkanes, alkenes and alkynes respectively.

 

• Tetravalent (Option B): Carbon's four valence electrons allow it to form four covalent bonds — a core reason for its versatility.

 

• Catenation (Option C): Carbon's self-linking ability, central to the diversity of organic compounds.

question: If a conductor has a resistance of 10 Ω and a potential difference of 5 V is applied across it, what is the current flowing through it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.5 A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Ohm's Law, the current (I) flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference (V) across it and inversely proportional to its resistance (R): I = V/R. (ओम का नियम — I = V/R)

 

• Here, V = 5 V and R = 10 Ω, so I = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

 

• Ohm's Law holds only for conductors kept at a constant temperature, and materials that obey it are called ohmic conductors (e.g., most metals); materials that don't (like diodes) are called non-ohmic.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistance (R) is measured in ohms (Ω) and represents the opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of current; it depends on the material, length, cross-sectional area and temperature of the conductor: R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity.

 

• For resistors in series, the equivalent resistance is the sum of individual resistances (R = R₁+R₂+...); for resistors in parallel, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of reciprocals (1/R = 1/R₁+1/R₂+...).

 

• Electric power dissipated in a resistor is given by P = VI = I²R = V²/R, measured in watts.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to compute R/V or V+R instead of V/R — always remember I = V/R as per Ohm's Law.

 

• 5 A (Option B) and 2 A (Option D) result from incorrect arithmetic (e.g., confusing which value to divide by which).

question: Which of the following is/are true about the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet? (i) The relative strength of the magnetic field is shown by the degree of closeness of the field lines. (ii) No two magnetic field lines can intersect each other.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both (i) and (ii).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct properties of magnetic field lines. (चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं के गुण)

 

• Statement (i) is correct: the degree of closeness of field lines indicates the relative strength of the magnetic field at that point — field lines are closer together near the poles (where the field is strong) and farther apart away from the poles (where the field is weaker).

 

• Statement (ii) is correct: no two magnetic field lines can ever intersect each other. If they did, it would mean the compass needle placed at that point of intersection could point in two different directions simultaneously, which is physically impossible — the magnetic field at any point has a single, unique direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet emerge from the North pole and merge into the South pole outside the magnet, while inside the magnet they run from the South pole to the North pole, forming continuous closed loops.

 

• The region around a magnet where its magnetic effect can be experienced is called the magnetic field; its SI unit is tesla (T).

 

• A compass needle aligns itself along the direction of the magnetic field at any given point, which is why compasses are used to trace and study magnetic field lines.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, C and D are incorrect because both given statements about magnetic field lines are factually accurate, not just one or neither.

question: The crystalline lens of the eye mainly helps in:
option_3: Providing fine adjustment of focal length
option_4: Controlling the amount of light entering the eye
solution_text:
The correct answer is Providing fine adjustment of focal length.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The crystalline lens of the eye is a transparent, flexible, convex structure that helps focus light onto the retina by fine-tuning its focal length, a process called accommodation. (नेत्र लेंस — फोकस दूरी का सूक्ष्म समायोजन)

 

• Accommodation is carried out with the help of the ciliary muscles: when these muscles contract, the lens becomes more curved (rounder) to focus on nearby objects; when they relax, the lens becomes thinner (flatter) to focus on distant objects.

 

• The lens works together with the cornea (which does most of the initial, fixed bending of light) to form a sharp image on the retina.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colour detection is performed by cone cells present in the retina, not by the lens.

 

• Sending signals to the brain is the job of the optic nerve, which carries electrical impulses generated by the retina to the visual cortex of the brain.

 

• The iris (a coloured, muscular diaphragm) controls the size of the pupil, thereby regulating the amount of light entering the eye.

 

NOTE

 

• Detecting colour of objects (Option A): Performed by cone cells in the retina.

 

• Sending signals to the brain (Option B): Performed by the optic nerve.

 

• Controlling the amount of light entering the eye (Option D): Performed by the iris and pupil, not the lens.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: Sound waves are transverse and need a medium.
option_2: Sound requires a medium to travel and is longitudinal.
option_3: Sound can travel in vacuum because it is longitudinal.
option_4: Sound travels faster in vacuum than in air.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sound requires a medium to travel and is longitudinal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth parallel to the direction in which the wave travels, producing regions of compression (high pressure) and rarefaction (low pressure). (ध्वनि — अनुदैर्ध्य तरंग, माध्यम आवश्यक)

 

• Being a mechanical wave, sound needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel, since it propagates through the vibration of the medium's particles — it cannot travel through vacuum, which has no particles to vibrate.

 

• The speed of sound is generally greatest in solids, less in liquids, and least in gases, because particles are packed closer together (and can transmit vibrations faster) in denser media.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Speed of sound in air ≈ 344 m/s (at about 22°C); in water ≈ 1,500 m/s; in steel ≈ 5,960 m/s.

 

• Light, unlike sound, is an electromagnetic (transverse) wave and can travel through vacuum, which is why we can see the Sun and stars but famously cannot hear sound in outer space.

 

• The human audible range is 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; below this is infrasonic and above is ultrasonic.

 

NOTE

 

• Sound waves are transverse (Option A): Incorrect — sound waves are longitudinal, not transverse (transverse waves are characteristic of light and other EM waves, and of waves on a stretched string).

 

• Sound can travel in vacuum (Option C) and sound travels faster in vacuum than in air (Option D): Both incorrect — sound cannot travel through vacuum at all, since it needs a material medium.

question: What is the mass number of a neutral atom with 11 electrons, 11 protons and 12 neutrons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mass number (A) of an atom is defined as the total number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus (also called nucleons): Mass number = Number of protons + Number of neutrons. (द्रव्यमान संख्या = प्रोटॉन + न्यूट्रॉन)

 

• Here, number of protons = 11 and number of neutrons = 12, so Mass number = 11 + 12 = 23.

 

• Since the atom is neutral, the number of electrons (11) equals the number of protons (11) — this is why electrons don't count toward mass number, as their mass is negligible (about 1/1836th of a proton's mass).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The atomic number (Z) equals the number of protons (or electrons in a neutral atom) and defines the identity of the element — here, Z = 11, which corresponds to sodium (Na).

 

• Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but different mass numbers (i.e., different numbers of neutrons); this particular atom, sodium-23, is the only stable, naturally-occurring isotope of sodium.

 

• Standard notation: an atom is written as _Z^A X, e.g., sodium here would be written ₁₁²³Na.

 

NOTE

 

• 12 (Option B) is just the number of neutrons alone.

 

• 22 (Option C) and 11 (Option D) do not match the correct sum of protons and neutrons; 11 is simply the number of protons (or electrons).

question: Which of the following functions is NOT associated with Golgi Complex?
option_1: It modifies and packages proteins received from the endoplasmic reticulum.
option_2: It transports and secretes materials outside the cell.
option_3: It forms lysosomes that help in intracellular digestion.
option_4: It permits entries and exits of substances from the cell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It permits entries and exits of substances from the cell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golgi Complex (Golgi apparatus/body) is a cell organelle made of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae, and its main functions are modification, packaging, sorting and transport of proteins and lipids — it is often called the "packaging and dispatch centre" of the cell. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — संशोधन एवं पैकेजिंग केंद्र)

 

• Controlling the entry and exit of substances into and out of the cell is the job of the plasma membrane (cell membrane), which is selectively permeable, not the Golgi complex.

 

• The Golgi complex is a central hub in the endomembrane system, working closely with the endoplasmic reticulum to process molecules synthesised by the cell.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Golgi apparatus was discovered by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898, who was awarded the Nobel Prize for this discovery.

 

• Products modified in the Golgi complex are transported in vesicles, which bud off from one face (the cis face, facing the ER) and mature/exit from the other (the trans face).

 

• Lysosomes, often called the "suicide bags" of the cell, contain powerful digestive enzymes and are formed by the Golgi complex; they break down worn-out cell organelles, foreign particles and even the cell itself during certain processes.

 

NOTE

 

• Modifies and packages proteins from the ER (Option A): A core, well-established function of the Golgi complex.

 

• Transports and secretes materials outside the cell (Option B): A genuine Golgi function, via secretory vesicles.

 

• Forms lysosomes (Option C): A well-documented Golgi function — lysosomes bud off from the Golgi complex.

question: A car starts from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/hr in 20 seconds. What is the acceleration of the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 m/s².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v − u)/t, where u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, and t = time taken. (त्वरण = वेग परिवर्तन/समय)

 

• Convert final speed to SI units first: 72 km/hr = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

 

• Since the car starts from rest, u = 0 m/s, v = 20 m/s, and t = 20 s, so a = (20 − 0)/20 = 1 m/s².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Quick conversion trick: to convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18; to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

 

• If a body decelerates (slows down), its acceleration is negative, also called retardation or deceleration.

 

• The three standard equations of motion (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as) are used to relate velocity, acceleration, time and distance in problems of this type.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert speed to consistent SI units (m/s) before calculating acceleration in m/s²; mixing km/hr and seconds is a very common error.

question: The relationships of food chain, which can be shown as a series of branching lines is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Food web.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A food web is a network of interconnected food chains in an ecosystem, and it is typically represented as a series of branching lines showing the many possible feeding relationships between organisms, since most organisms eat, and are eaten by, more than one species. (खाद्य जाल — शाखाओं के रूप में दर्शाया गया)

 

• Unlike a simple food chain (a single, straight-line sequence of who-eats-whom), a food web captures the complexity and interdependence of real ecosystems, making it more ecologically realistic.

 

• Food webs help illustrate concepts like alternative food sources, and show why the loss of even one species can affect many others through multiple interconnected pathways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• A food chain shows a linear flow of energy: e.g., Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle, where each organism occupies one trophic level.

 

• Trophic levels classify organisms by their feeding position: Producers (Level 1, e.g., green plants), Primary consumers/herbivores (Level 2), Secondary consumers/carnivores (Level 3), and so on, up to top/apex predators.

 

• Energy transfer between trophic levels follows the 10% Law (Lindeman's Law): only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next, the rest being lost mainly as heat.

 

NOTE

 

• World wide web (Option B): An internet-based information system, unrelated to ecology.

 

• Spider web (Option C): A silk structure built by spiders to trap prey, unrelated to food chains.

 

• Trophic level (Option D): Refers to a single feeding position/step within a food chain, not the entire branching network.

question: What is the role of nitrogen gas in chip packets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is It prevents oxidation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitrogen gas (N₂) is filled into chip (and other snack) packets mainly because it is inert (chemically unreactive) — it displaces the oxygen inside the packet, thereby preventing oxidation of the fats/oils in the chips, which would otherwise turn rancid and spoil the taste and quality. (नाइट्रोजन — ऑक्सीकरण रोकथाम)

 

• Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the Earth's atmosphere, is colourless, odourless, tasteless, and does not react readily with food components, making it ideal for food packaging (modified atmosphere packaging).

 

• Besides preventing rancidity, the nitrogen cushion also provides physical protection, helping cushion the chips against breakage during handling and transport — though its primary chemical role tested here is preventing oxidation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Oxidation of fats (rancidity) occurs when oxygen reacts with the oils in food, producing unpleasant odours and flavours and reducing nutritional value; keeping oxygen out slows this process considerably.

 

• Nitrogen's inertness is also exploited in other applications: filling light bulbs, inflating aircraft and racing car tyres (as it expands less with heat than compressed air), and preserving other perishable foods.

 

• Nitrogen is obtained industrially mainly by the fractional distillation of liquid air.

 

NOTE

 

• It absorbs moisture (Option A): This is the role of desiccants like silica gel packets, not nitrogen gas.

 

• It adds crispiness (Option C): Crispiness comes from the cooking/frying process and low moisture content of the chips themselves, not from the nitrogen atmosphere.

 

• It adds flavour (Option D): Nitrogen is inert and tasteless; it does not contribute any flavour to the food.

question: The marked price of an item is set at 49% above its cost price. If the merchant sells the item at 16% below the marked price, his profit percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 25.2%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = 149% of Cost Price (CP); Selling Price (SP) = 84% of MP (16% below MP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let CP = 100. Then MP = 100 × 1.49 = 149.

 

• SP = MP × (1 − 16/100) = 149 × 0.84 = 125.16.

 

• Profit% = (SP − CP)/CP × 100 = (125.16 − 100)/100 × 100 = 25.16% ≈ 25.2%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net % change = 49 + (−16) + (49 × −16)/100 = 49 − 16 − 7.84 = 25.16% ≈ 25.2% (successive percentage change formula).

 

NOTE

 

• Use the successive percentage change formula x + y + xy/100 whenever a value undergoes two percentage changes one after another (here, +49% then −16%).

question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 10 and 12 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 6 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 30 minutes. Find the capacity of the tank.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 40 gallons.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pipe A fills the tank in 10 min, Pipe B in 12 min; waste pipe C empties 6 gallons/min. All three together fill the tank in 30 min.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the capacity of the tank be C gallons. Rate of A = C/10 gallons/min, rate of B = C/12 gallons/min, rate of C = −6 gallons/min.

 

• Combined rate = C/30 gallons/min (since together they fill it in 30 min).

 

• C/10 + C/12 − 6 = C/30. Multiplying throughout by 60: 6C + 5C − 360 = 2C.

 

• 11C − 360 = 2C ⟹ 9C = 360 ⟹ C = 40 gallons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up the equation directly in terms of the unknown capacity and clear all fractions by multiplying by the LCM of the times involved (here, LCM of 10, 12, 30 = 60) — this avoids working with fractions throughout.

 

NOTE

 

• The waste pipe's rate is always subtracted (negative), since it works against the filling pipes.

question: A vendor bought 100 dozens of bananas for ₹4,800 and sold them at 4 bananas for ₹20. Find his gain percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• 100 dozens (= 1,200 bananas) bought for ₹4,800; sold at 4 bananas for ₹20.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Cost price per banana = 4,800 ÷ 1,200 = ₹4.

 

• Selling price per banana = 20 ÷ 4 = ₹5.

 

• Gain% = (SP − CP)/CP × 100 = (5 − 4)/4 × 100 = 25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always convert bulk buy/sell rates to a per-unit cost and selling price first — comparing per-unit values makes the profit% calculation immediate.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 dozen = 12, so 100 dozens = 1,200 bananas — don't forget this conversion.

question: From the top of a 42 m high building, the angle of depression of a man on the ground is 30°. How far is the man from the base of the building? (Take √3 = 1.7321 and round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 72.75 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Height of building = 42 m; angle of depression of the man from the top = 30°; √3 = 1.7321.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the man's position (alternate angles), so tan 30° = height/distance.

 

• Distance = height ÷ tan 30° = height × √3 = 42 × 1.7321.

 

• 42 × 1.7321 = 72.7482 ≈ 72.75 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a 30° angle of elevation/depression, distance = height × √3 directly (since tan 30° = 1/√3); for 60°, distance = height/√3; for 45°, distance = height.

 

NOTE

 

• Always draw the right triangle: the building is the perpendicular, the ground distance is the base, and the line of sight is the hypotenuse — the angle of depression from the top always equals the angle of elevation from the ground point, by the alternate angle property of parallel lines.

question: Which of the following numbers is the largest number between 4000 and 5000 that is completely divisible by 42?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4998.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find the largest multiple of 42 that lies between 4000 and 5000.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Divide 5000 by 42: 5000 ÷ 42 = 119.04 (approx), so the largest whole multiplier is 119.

 

• 42 × 119 = 4998, which lies between 4000 and 5000.

 

• Check: 42 × 120 = 5040, which exceeds 5000, so 119 is indeed the largest valid multiplier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Divide the upper limit by the divisor, take the integer (floor) part, and multiply back by the divisor: floor(5000/42) × 42 = 119 × 42 = 4998.

 

NOTE

 

• Quick check: 4998 ÷ 42 = 119 exactly (no remainder), confirming complete divisibility; also verify 4998 > 4000 to ensure it lies within the required range.

question: If the ratio of two numbers is 8 : 7, and their HCF is 30, then their LCM is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 1680.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ratio of two numbers = 8 : 7; HCF of the two numbers = 30.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since the ratio is 8:7 (co-prime to each other), the numbers can be written as 8×30 = 240 and 7×30 = 210.

 

• For numbers of the form a×h and b×h where a, b are co-prime, LCM = a × b × h (HCF).

 

• LCM = 8 × 7 × 30 = 1,680.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever two numbers are in ratio a:b (a, b co-prime) with HCF = h, their LCM is always a × b × h directly — no need to separately compute the actual numbers and then find LCM.

 

NOTE

 

• This shortcut only works when the ratio terms a and b are already co-prime (which 8 and 7 are, having no common factor).

question: If 2a + b + c = 0 and 8a³ + b³ + c³ = kabc, then find the value of k².
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 36.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2a + b + c = 0 and 8a³ + b³ + c³ = kabc.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let x = 2a, y = b, z = c. Then x + y + z = 2a + b + c = 0 (given), and x³ + y³ + z³ = (2a)³ + b³ + c³ = 8a³ + b³ + c³.

 

• Standard identity: if x + y + z = 0, then x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz.

 

• So 8a³ + b³ + c³ = 3 × (2a) × b × c = 6abc.

 

• Comparing with kabc, we get k = 6, so k² = 36.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a sum of three terms is zero, immediately apply the identity x³+y³+z³ = 3xyz — this converts a cubic expression into a simple product, avoiding lengthy expansion.

 

NOTE

 

• The key step is recognising that 8a³ = (2a)³, allowing the substitution x = 2a so that the given condition 2a+b+c=0 becomes x+y+z=0 directly.

question: The average age of 20 students of a class is 29 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 30 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 50 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 20 students = 29 years; including the teacher, average of 21 people = 30 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 20 students = 20 × 29 = 580 years.

 

• Sum of ages of 20 students + teacher = 21 × 30 = 630 years.

 

• Teacher's age = 630 − 580 = 50 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• New person's value = New average + (old count × increase in average) = 30 + (20 × 1) = 50 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert averages to totals (sum = average × count) before adding or removing a member — working directly with averages easily leads to errors.

question: Simplify: −5 × [−4 × {−3 − (2×(−3)×(−4) + 5×6) − 3} ÷ (−20×3)] × 0.5/(2×5)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• −5 × [−4 × {−3 − (2×(−3)×(−4) + 5×6) − 3} ÷ (−20×3)] × 0.5/(2×5) = ?

 

SOLUTION (work from the innermost bracket outward)

 

• Innermost: (2×(−3)×(−4) + 5×6) = (24 + 30) = 54.

 

• Curly bracket: {−3 − 54 − 3} = −60.

 

• Square bracket: −4 × (−60) ÷ (−20×3) = 240 ÷ (−60) = −4.

 

• Now: −5 × (−4) × 0.5/(2×5) = 20 × 0.5/10 = 20 × 0.05 = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Solve strictly innermost-bracket-first (round → curly → square), and handle the final ×0.5÷10 as a single multiplication by 0.05 to avoid arithmetic slips.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake here is misreading '÷(−20×3)' as '+(−20×3)' — read the operator before each bracket carefully; here it is division, not addition.

question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 40°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 3 : 5, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 20°.

 

GIVEN

 

• Bisectors of ∠R and ∠S of quadrilateral PQRS meet at T; ∠STR = 40°; ∠P : ∠Q = 3 : 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard result: in a quadrilateral, if the bisectors of two adjacent angles (here R and S) meet at T, then ∠RTS = 90° − (∠P + ∠Q)/2... Let's derive it directly: in triangle RTS, ∠TRS = ∠R/2, ∠TSR = ∠S/2, so ∠RTS = 180° − (∠R + ∠S)/2.

 

• 40° = 180° − (∠R + ∠S)/2 ⟹ (∠R + ∠S)/2 = 140° ⟹ ∠R + ∠S = 280°.

 

• Sum of all angles of a quadrilateral = 360°, so ∠P + ∠Q = 360° − 280° = 80°.

 

• ∠P : ∠Q = 3 : 5 (8 parts = 80°) ⟹ 1 part = 10°, so ∠P = 30°, ∠Q = 50°.

 

• Difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 50° − 30° = 20°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the direct formula: if bisectors of ∠R and ∠S of a quadrilateral meet at T, then ∠R + ∠S = 2(180° − ∠RTS), letting you jump straight from ∠RTS to ∠R+∠S, and hence to ∠P+∠Q via the angle sum property.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse this with the analogous triangle-bisector formula (∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2); the quadrilateral version is different because the angle sum is 360°, not 180°.

question: The marks obtained by 15 students out of a maximum of 26 in a test are given as 14, 12, 17, 16, 19, 13, 14, 15, 11, 23, 16, 22, 21, 18, and 25. Find the product of the possible modes of this set of data.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 224.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marks: 14, 12, 17, 16, 19, 13, 14, 15, 11, 23, 16, 22, 21, 18, 25 (15 values).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Count the frequency of each value: 14 appears twice (2 times), 16 appears twice (2 times); every other value (12, 17, 19, 13, 15, 11, 23, 22, 21, 18, 25) appears only once.

 

• Since 14 and 16 both occur the maximum number of times (twice each), this is a bimodal data set with modes 14 and 16.

 

• Product of the modes = 14 × 16 = 224.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When asked for the 'product of possible modes', first carefully tally frequencies — a data set can have more than one mode (bimodal/multimodal) if two or more values tie for the highest frequency.

 

NOTE

 

• Mode = the value(s) that occur most frequently in a data set; it is different from mean (average) and median (middle value when arranged in order).

question: A number is increased by 15% and the resulting number is again increased by 10%. What is the overall percentage increase in the number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 26.5%.

 

GIVEN

 

• A number is increased successively by 15% and then by 10%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using the successive percentage change formula: Overall % change = x + y + xy/100, where x = 15, y = 10.

 

• Overall % change = 15 + 10 + (15×10)/100 = 25 + 1.5 = 26.5%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take the number as 100: after +15% it becomes 115; after a further +10% it becomes 115 × 1.10 = 126.5, an increase of 26.5 from 100, i.e. 26.5%.

 

NOTE

 

• Never simply add the two percentages (15% + 10% = 25%) when changes are applied successively (one after another) rather than to the same original base — always account for the compounding cross-term xy/100.

question: An amount of ₹4328 is divided among A, B, C and D in such a way that the shares of A and B, B and C, and C and D are in the ratios of 4 : 5, 4 : 5 and 6 : 7, respectively. The share of A (in ₹) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹768.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total amount = ₹4,328; A:B = 4:5, B:C = 4:5, C:D = 6:7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let A = 4x, B = 5x (from A:B = 4:5).

 

• From B:C = 4:5, C = B × 5/4 = 5x × 5/4 = 25x/4.

 

• From C:D = 6:7, D = C × 7/6 = (25x/4) × 7/6 = 175x/24.

 

• Express all in terms of x/24: A = 96x/24, B = 120x/24, C = 150x/24, D = 175x/24.

 

• Sum = (96+120+150+175)x/24 = 541x/24 = 4,328 ⟹ x = 4,328 × 24/541 = 8 × 24 = 192 (since 4,328 ÷ 541 = 8).

 

• A's share = 4x = 4 × 192 = ₹768.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain the ratios by making the common term (B, then C) match: A:B:C:D = 96:120:150:175 directly (in the smallest whole-number form), then divide the total in this ratio.

 

NOTE

 

• When combining chained ratios (A:B, B:C, C:D), always scale each ratio so the shared term (B, then C) has the same value before combining them into a single four-term ratio.

question: Rahul is 5 years younger than his sister. After 3 years, the sum of their ages will be 35 years. Find Rahul's present age.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 12 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Rahul is 5 years younger than his sister; after 3 years, sum of their ages = 35 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Rahul's present age = R years; sister's present age = (R + 5) years.

 

• After 3 years: Rahul's age = R + 3, sister's age = R + 5 + 3 = R + 8.

 

• Sum after 3 years: (R + 3) + (R + 8) = 35 ⟹ 2R + 11 = 35 ⟹ 2R = 24 ⟹ R = 12 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Sum of ages after n years = (sum of present ages) + 2n (since both people age by n years). Here, present sum = 35 − 2×3 = 29, and since Rahul = sister − 5, present sum = 2×sister − 5 = 29 ⟹ sister = 17, Rahul = 12.

 

NOTE

 

• Always add the SAME number of years to both people's ages when the question says 'after n years' — a common mistake is adding it only once instead of to both individuals.

question: Two trains 285 metres and 235 metres long are running in the opposite direction with speeds of 61 km/hr and 83 km/hr, respectively. In how much time will the first train cross the second?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 13 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train lengths: 285 m and 235 m; speeds: 61 km/hr and 83 km/hr, moving in opposite directions.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance to be covered while crossing = sum of lengths = 285 + 235 = 520 m.

 

• Since the trains move in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of speeds = 61 + 83 = 144 km/hr.

 

• Convert to m/s: 144 × 5/18 = 40 m/s.

 

• Time = distance/speed = 520/40 = 13 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For crossing problems: opposite direction ⟹ relative speed = sum of speeds; same direction ⟹ relative speed = difference of speeds. Total distance to cover always = sum of the two train lengths (when two moving trains cross each other).

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert km/hr to m/s (multiply by 5/18) before working with lengths given in metres and time in seconds.

question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 6 and 10 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 5 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• A, B, C complete one unit of work alone in 3, 6, 10 days respectively; find time to complete 3 times the work together.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take total work = LCM(3, 6, 10) = 30 units.

 

• A's rate = 30/3 = 10 units/day; B's rate = 30/6 = 5 units/day; C's rate = 30/10 = 3 units/day.

 

• Combined rate = 10 + 5 + 3 = 18 units/day.

 

• Time for 1× work = 30/18 days. Time for 3× work = (3 × 30)/18 = 90/18 = 5 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take total work as the LCM of the individual times — this converts all rates to whole numbers, making combined-rate calculations quick and error-free.

 

NOTE

 

• For 'n times the work', simply multiply the total work (or the final time) by n; don't recompute individual rates.

question: A purse has ₹1 and ₹2 coins in the ratio 3 : 2. If the total amount of money is ₹70, how many coins are there in total?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 50.

 

GIVEN

 

• ₹1 and ₹2 coins are in ratio 3:2; total amount = ₹70.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number of ₹1 coins = 3x and ₹2 coins = 2x.

 

• Total value = 3x × 1 + 2x × 2 = 3x + 4x = 7x.

 

• 7x = 70 ⟹ x = 10.

 

• Total number of coins = 3x + 2x = 5x = 5 × 10 = 50.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Compute the 'value per ratio-unit' first: value of coins in ratio 3:2 (₹1, ₹2 coins) per unit x = 3(1) + 2(2) = 7; then x = total amount ÷ 7, and total coins = (sum of ratio terms) × x.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'number of coins in ratio' with 'value of coins in ratio' — the value contributed by each coin type must be multiplied by its face value before adding.

question: A motorist travels a total distance of 30 km in 50 minutes. He drives at a speed of x km/hr for the first 11 minutes, then at 2x km/hr for the next 25 minutes, and finally at x km/hr for the remaining part of the journey. Find the value of x.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 24.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total distance = 30 km in 50 minutes; speeds x, 2x, x km/hr for 11 min, 25 min, and the remaining time.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Remaining time = 50 − 11 − 25 = 14 minutes.

 

• Distance = speed × time; converting minutes to hours (divide by 60): Distance = x×(11/60) + 2x×(25/60) + x×(14/60).

 

• = x/60 × (11 + 50 + 14) = x/60 × 75 = 75x/60 = 1.25x.

 

• Set equal to 30: 1.25x = 30 ⟹ x = 24.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine all time-segments into a single 'effective x-multiple': here total = x×(11 + 2×25 + 14)/60 = x×75/60, letting you solve directly for x in one step without separately computing each leg's distance.

 

NOTE

 

• Always keep time in consistent units (convert minutes to hours) when speed is given in km/hr.

question: A hemisphere has radius 3.5 cm. If total surface area of hemisphere is equal to the surface area of a sphere, then what is the volume of the sphere? (Take π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 539√3/8 cm³.

 

GIVEN

 

• Radius of hemisphere, r = 3.5 cm; Total Surface Area of hemisphere = Surface Area of a sphere of radius R; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• TSA of hemisphere = 3πr² (curved surface 2πr² + base πr²). Surface area of sphere = 4πR².

 

• Setting them equal: 3πr² = 4πR² ⟹ R² = 3r²/4.

 

• r = 7/2, so r² = 49/4. R² = 3 × (49/4)/4 = 147/16.

 

• Volume of sphere = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)πR²×R = (4/3) × (22/7) × (147/16) × √(147/16).

 

• √147 = 7√3, so √(147/16) = 7√3/4. Now: (4/3)×(22/7)×(147/16)×(7√3/4) = 539√3/8 cm³ (after simplification).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First reduce the relation 3r² = 4R² to get R² in terms of r² directly, then substitute into V = (4/3)πR³ — keep everything in fraction/surd form (avoid decimals) since the answer options are in surd (√3) form.

 

NOTE

 

• TSA of a hemisphere = 3πr² (this includes the flat circular base); if only the curved surface were meant, it would be 2πr² — read the question carefully to know which is intended.

question: The income of Raman is ₹50,400. He saves 7.5% of his income. If his income increases by 26% and expenditure increases by 45%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. decrease by ₹7,875.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹50,400; savings = 7.5% of income; new income increases by 26%; new expenditure increases by 45%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Original savings = 7.5% of 50,400 = ₹3,780. Original expenditure = 50,400 − 3,780 = ₹46,620.

 

• New income = 50,400 × 1.26 = ₹63,504.

 

• New expenditure = 46,620 × 1.45 = ₹67,599.

 

• New savings = New income − New expenditure = 63,504 − 67,599 = −₹4,095 (a deficit).

 

• Change in savings = New savings − Old savings = −4,095 − 3,780 = −₹7,875, i.e. a decrease of ₹7,875.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always compute Income, Expenditure and Savings as three separate values first (Savings = Income − Expenditure); apply the respective % change to Income and Expenditure individually, then find the new Savings by subtraction — never apply a single % change directly to Savings.

 

NOTE

 

• A negative 'new savings' value simply means the person now spends more than they earn (a deficit) — this is a valid and common twist in such problems, and the change is still measured as (new − old).

question: If p : q : r = 13 : 5 : 14 and r : s = 42 : 3, then what is the value of p : q : r : s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 39:15:42:3.

 

GIVEN

 

• p : q : r = 13 : 5 : 14; r : s = 42 : 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• To combine, make the value of r equal in both ratios. In the first ratio, r = 14; in the second, r = 42. LCM of 14 and 42 = 42.

 

• Multiply the first ratio (p:q:r = 13:5:14) by 3 (so that r becomes 42): p:q:r = 39:15:42.

 

• The second ratio r:s = 42:3 already has r = 42, matching directly.

 

• Combined: p : q : r : s = 39 : 15 : 42 : 3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When combining chained ratios, always scale each ratio so that the common term (here, r) has the same value in both — using the LCM of the two given values of the common term makes the scaling factor a whole number.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check by verifying the shared term (r) is identical across the final combined ratio before finalising the answer.

question: Smart Bazaar is offering 'Buy 14, Get 11 free' on household items. What is the net percentage discount being offered by the Smart Bazaar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 44%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Offer: 'Buy 14, Get 11 free', i.e. pay for 14 items but receive 14 + 11 = 25 items.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Net discount % = (Free items)/(Total items received) × 100 = 11/(14+11) × 100 = 11/25 × 100 = 44%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For any 'Buy m, Get n free' offer, the discount % = n/(m+n) × 100 directly — no need to assume a price and compute separately.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is calculating discount as (free items)/(paid items) = 11/14, instead of (free items)/(total items received) = 11/25 — the discount is always on the total value received, not just the paid portion.

question: To buy furniture for a new apartment, Chang borrowed ₹50,000 at 16% per annum simple interest for 18 months. How much interest will she pay?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹12,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal (P) = ₹50,000; Rate (R) = 16% per annum; Time (T) = 18 months = 1.5 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simple Interest formula: SI = (P × R × T)/100.

 

• SI = (50,000 × 16 × 1.5)/100 = (50,000 × 24)/100 = 12,00,000/100 = ₹12,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always convert the time period into years before applying the SI formula, since the rate is given per annum — here, 18 months = 1.5 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Simple Interest formula: SI = PRT/100; Amount = Principal + Simple Interest.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 96, then the result is the same number. 60% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number, when added to 96, gives back the same number.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number = N. Then 0.2N + 96 = N.

 

• 96 = N − 0.2N = 0.8N ⟹ N = 96/0.8 = 120.

 

• 60% of N = 0.6 × 120 = 72.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'x% added to a number gives back the number' always means the added amount equals (100−x)% of the number; here, 96 = 80% of N, so N = 96 × (100/80) = 120 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse '20% of N added to 96 equals N' with '20% of N equals 96' — read the condition carefully before setting up the equation.

question: A rectangular box without a lid is made of thin sheet metal. The box has a length of 60 cm, a breadth of 40 cm, and a height of 30 cm. Find the total area of the sheet metal used to make the box and the cost of the sheet if 1 m² costs ₹50.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹42.

 

GIVEN

 

• Length (l) = 60 cm, breadth (b) = 40 cm, height (h) = 30 cm; box has no lid (open top); cost = ₹50 per m².

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since there's no lid, total sheet area = base + 4 side walls = lb + 2(lh) + 2(bh).

 

• = (60×40) + 2×(60×30) + 2×(40×30) = 2,400 + 3,600 + 2,400 = 8,400 cm².

 

• Convert to m²: 8,400 cm² = 8,400/10,000 = 0.84 m² (since 1 m² = 10,000 cm²).

 

• Cost = 0.84 × ₹50 = ₹42.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For an open (lidless) box, remember the area formula is lb + 2h(l+b) — one base area, plus four walls grouped as 2h(l+b); this is one full face (top) less than a fully closed cuboid's total surface area (2(lb+bh+hl)).

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert cm² to m² (divide by 10,000) before applying a per-m² cost rate — a very common source of error in mensuration-with-cost problems.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

612 610 620 617 627 623 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 633.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 612, 610, 620, 617, 627, 623, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 610−612=−2, 620−610=+10, 617−620=−3, 627−617=+10, 623−627=−4, ?−623=+10.

 

• The pattern alternates: the 'down' steps go −2, −3, −4, ... (increasing by 1 each time), while every 'up' step is a constant +10.

 

• Since the last given step (623 to ?) follows a −4 step, it must be an 'up' step of +10: ? = 623 + 10 = 633.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In alternating series, split the sequence into two groups (odd positions and even positions) and find the pattern in each group separately — here every alternate 'up' jump is fixed at +10.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute the full list of consecutive differences first before trying to spot the pattern — jumping to conclusions from just the first two terms is a common mistake.

question: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting in a row, facing the north. Only one person sits to the right of E. Only three people sit between G and E. Only three people sit between A and D, neither of whom sits on the left end. F sits immediately to the right of C. Only one person sits between A and B. Who sits second to the left of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. G.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people A–G in a row (positions 1 to 7 from left), facing north.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only one person sits to the right of E' ⟹ E is at position 6 (leaving exactly 1 seat, position 7, to its right).

 

• 'Only three people sit between G and E' ⟹ |pos(G) − 6| = 4 ⟹ G = 2 (position 10 is invalid).

 

• 'Only three people sit between A and D, neither of whom sits at the left end' ⟹ |pos(A) − pos(D)| = 4, and neither = position 1. From the remaining positions {1,3,4,5,7}, the only pair 4 apart excluding position 1 is (3,7). So {A, D} = {3, 7}.

 

• 'F sits immediately to the right of C' ⟹ F = C + 1. Remaining positions {1,4,5} are left for B, C, F; testing C=4, F=5 works, leaving B=1.

 

• 'Only one person sits between A and B' ⟹ |pos(A) − 1| = 2 ⟹ pos(A) = 3, so D = 7.

 

• Final arrangement (positions 1–7): B, G, A, C, F, E, D.

 

• Second to the left of C (position 4) is position 2 = G.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In seating puzzles, always fix the most restrictive clue first (like 'only one person to the right of E', which pins an exact position), then work outward step by step using the remaining clues.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only three people sit between X and Y' always means the positions of X and Y differ by exactly 4 (3 people occupy the seats strictly between them).

question:
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

IGP 3 KIO -10 MKN -23 OMM -36 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. QOL -49.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: IGP 3, KIO −10, MKN −23, OMM −36, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: I(9), K(11), M(13), O(15), → +2 each time → next = Q(17).

 

• 2nd letters: G(7), I(9), K(11), M(13), → +2 each time → next = O(15).

 

• 3rd letters: P(16), O(15), N(14), M(13), → −1 each time → next = L(12).

 

• So the next letter-cluster = QOL.

 

• Numbers: 3, −10, −23, −36, ? — differences are −13, −13, −13 → next = −36 − 13 = −49.

 

• Combined answer = QOL -49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a compound series (letters + numbers) into separate sub-series and solve each independently: track the 1st, 2nd, 3rd letters as three separate alphabet sequences, and the numbers as their own arithmetic sequence.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet positions (A=1...Z=26) before checking for a pattern — spotting a +2, +2, −1 letter-wise pattern is much easier numerically.

question:
Select the pair which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two set of pairs given below. Both pairs follow the same pattern.

KJL−NMO

LKM−ONP
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. VUW-YXZ.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern pairs: KJL–NMO and LKM–ONP.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check letter-by-letter shift from the first cluster to the second: K(+3)=N, J(+3)=M, L(+3)=O — confirmed by KJL→NMO.

 

• Second pair confirms it: L(+3)=O, K(+3)=N, M(+3)=P — LKM→ONP. So the rule is: add 3 to each letter.

 

• Test option D, VUW–YXZ: V(22)+3=25=Y ✓, U(21)+3=24=X ✓, W(23)+3=26=Z ✓ — all three letters match exactly.

 

• (The other options fail this check on at least one letter, e.g. Option A's V+3=Y✓ but T+3=W≠X.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For letter-cluster pair analogies, convert each letter to its alphabet number and check if a constant shift (here, +3) applies to all three positions consistently — test the full three-letter set, not just the first letter.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the pattern using BOTH given example pairs before applying it to the options, to rule out coincidental single-pair matches.

question:
Select the pair which follows the same pattern as that followed by the two set of pairs given below. Both pairs follow the same pattern.

KGD−AWT

FBY−VRO
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. XTQ-NJG.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pattern pairs: KGD–AWT and FBY–VRO.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter shift: K(11)→A(1): 11+16=27≡1 (mod 26), i.e. add 16 (or equivalently subtract 10) cyclically.

 

• Confirm with the rest: G(7)+16=23=W ✓; D(4)+16=20=T ✓ (matches AWT). And F(6)+16=22=V ✓; B(2)+16=18=R ✓; Y(25)+16=41≡15=O ✓ (matches VRO).

 

• So the rule is: add 16 (mod 26) to each letter, equivalent to subtracting 10 cyclically.

 

• Test option D, XTQ–NJG: X(24)+16=40≡14=N ✓, T(20)+16=36≡10=J ✓, Q(17)+16=33≡7=G ✓ — all match.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a simple constant shift doesn't work directly (goes past Z), always check with mod 26 wraparound — many letter-shift patterns cycle back to the start of the alphabet.

 

NOTE

 

• Adding 16 is mathematically the same as subtracting 10 (since 16 ≡ −10 mod 26) — whichever is easier to compute mentally for a given letter can be used.

question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

28 + 11 − 3 ÷ 45 × 9 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 0.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol substitutions: + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +.

 

• Expression: 28 + 11 − 3 ÷ 45 × 9 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its actual meaning: 28 − 11 × 3 + 45 ÷ 9 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS on the converted expression: 45 ÷ 9 = 5; 11 × 3 = 33.

 

• Now: 28 − 33 + 5 = −5 + 5 = 0.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the ENTIRE expression with the real operations substituted in, then apply BODMAS normally — do not try to calculate while substituting symbol-by-symbol, as this causes order-of-operation errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check each symbol substitution against the given key before starting the calculation; a single wrong substitution changes the entire answer.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for 'x', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', what will come in place of question mark (?) in the following equation?

11 D 30 C 42 A 3 B 4 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 37.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −.

 

• Expression: 11 D 30 C 42 A 3 B 4 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the meanings: 11 − 30 + 42 ÷ 3 × 4 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: 42 ÷ 3 = 14; 14 × 4 = 56.

 

• Now: 11 − 30 + 56 = −19 + 56 = 37.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write out the letter-to-symbol key clearly on scratch paper first, then substitute all symbols in one pass before calculating — this avoids confusing which letter maps to which operation mid-calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Division and multiplication are always performed before addition and subtraction, regardless of the order they appear in the (substituted) expression.

question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single-digit numbers only. (Counting to be done from left to right only)

(Left) 6 3 6 9 9 4 4 1 7 5 6 2 1 6 6 6 8 8 2 9 1 5 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 6 3 6 9 9 4 4 1 7 5 6 2 1 6 6 6 8 8 2 9 1 5 (22 digits, positions 1–22).

 

SOLUTION

 

• We need an odd digit at position i such that: digit(i−1) is odd AND digit(i+1) is even.
